title: Entropy-aware token provenance and deterministic replay crediting for streaming fragments
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Background: We continue to see rare but actionable divergences between tokenized counts emitted by the tokenizer service and the final billing ledger for long-running streaming sessions that involve client-side chunk coalescing, speculative replay, or prefix reuse after midstream fallback. Root cause summary: small input fragments with low-entropy boundaries (e.g., repeated separator tokens, JSON-ish payloads, or base64-encoded binary attachments) can be coalesced differently by clients or proxies; speculative replay/resume paths produce duplicate fragments without a stable provenance identifier; rate-limiter windows combined with optimistic finalization can result in double-crediting or missed backfills. This ticket introduces a deterministic, entropy-aware token provenance scheme so fragments can be credited idempotently, and implements a reconciliation path to retroactively adjust credits when speculative or duplicate fragments are observed.
acceptance_criteria: Every input fragment accepted by the public ingestion layer carries a deterministic provenance id (string) derived from content length and a stable hash; provenance id persists across retries/resumes
The tokenizer service emits per-fragment token_count and provenance_id with each partial streaming delta; the metering pipeline uses provenance_id for idempotent finalization
Speculative replay or resume of fragments does not increase final billed tokens beyond a 0.1% statistical baseline for fuzzed workloads (benchmark harness run)
Rate-limiter integration: transient retries within a configurable grace window are pre-authorized and do not result in duplicate, permanent ledger debits
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) covering: client coalescing, websocket reconnect + resume, midstream model fallback with prefix reuse, and base64-attachment edge cases
Rollout toggle (server-side flag) and monitoring dashboards with quick-compare metrics (token delta per-session, dedupe rate, billing drift) are in place before rollout to prod
technical_notes: Provenance id spec: provenance = base32(murmur3_128(length || first-64-bytes || shannon_entropy_estimate)) to avoid exposing raw payloads yet remain stable across equivalent encodings
Entropy estimator: approximate shannon using 256-bin byte-frequency sketch to cheaply detect low-entropy blobs (e.g., repeated separators or long padding sequences)

Token attribution: tokenizer emits (provenance, token_count, byte_count, encoding_hint) on each partial delta; metering pipeline keeps last-finalized-offset per-provenance to support idempotent finalization
Ledger model change: add provenance_id string column + last_finalized_offset + speculative_flag; write-path must be idempotent on (tenant_id, provenance_id, offset_range)
Backfill reconciliation: a background job will scan for duplicate provenance writes and perform compensating transactions (retrodictive credits) tagged with audit_reason
Performance budget: provenance computation must add <0.6ms average to ingestion path; use vectorized murmur and approximate entropy to meet target
Security/privacy: provenance is a non-reversible fingerprint; avoid including long raw prefixes or secrets. Conform to existing PII handling rules.
steps: 1) Investigate: run sampling job over last 90 days to enumerate frequency of ambiguous fragment coalescing and quantify impact (done: sampling attached in Confluence)
2) Design: finalize provenance id format and ledger schema changes (doc: confluence.redwood.internal/metering/provenance-spec)
3) Prototype: implement provenance in ingestion-api and tokenizer-service behind feature flag; add emission to streaming deltas
4) Ledger schema migration: add columns (provenance_id, last_finalized_offset, speculative_flag); add idempotent upsert path
5) Integration: wire metering pipeline to use provenance for finalization and de-dup logic; add rate-limiter grace-window hook
6) Test: unit + integration harness using fuzzed clients that coalesce/split chunks, simulate reconnect/resume and midstream model fallback
7) Observability: add dashboards and alerts, run canary with 5% of traffic, compare billed vs. emitted tokens
8) Rollout: progressive ramp with kill-switch; run reconciliation job for 30d window after rollout
9) Postmortem: monitor for anomalies for 90d, capture lessons in ticket and update docs
